fact: The National Payment Systems (Consumer Protection) Regulations, 2022 (S.I. 103), made by the Finance Minister on 12 July 2022 and gazetted 9 September 2022, set conduct, disclosure and complaint rules for payment licensees.
The regulations let a consumer unsatisfied with a licensee's decision lodge a complaint with the Central Bank, which must determine it within 21 working days and may order refund or compensation.

Uganda's National Payment Systems Act 2020 (commenced 4 September 2020) s.65 requires payment service providers to comply with consumer protection requirements prescribed by the Bank of Uganda, and s.65(3)-(4) bars misleading advertising or offering unapproved services, an offence carrying a fine of up to 350 currency points or up to two years' imprisonment.

The Bank of Uganda runs a Financial Consumer Empowerment Mechanism that takes customer complaints about supervised financial institutions after 21 days without a satisfactory answer from the institution, guided by the Mobile Money Guidelines 2013 among others.

UNCDF says the Bank of Uganda updated its National Payments Act in 2022 to include financial consumer protection provisions, alongside the 2011 Financial Consumer Protection Guidelines for institutions licensed under the Financial Institutions Act.

The Uganda Microfinance Regulatory Authority launched its Digital Lending Guidelines Vol.1 (2024) in March 2024, setting conduct rules for online lenders, including confidentiality, interest limits, no harassment and a complaints redress mechanism.
Umra officials said the authority had received multiple complaints from clients about licensed digital lenders still harassing them.
